one_liner: AVX2 split-block Bloom filter: one 32-byte block per key, about 2-3x faster queries than a standard Bloom filter.
what_it_does: A header-only, insert-only approximate-membership filter over uint64_t keys (SimdBlockFilter<HashFamily> in src/simd-block.h), copied from Apache Impala into the cuckoo filter repo in Dec 2016. You construct it with log2 of the heap bytes to use, then call Add(key) and Find(key). Find can return false positives but never false negatives. It is not a drop-in for a Bloom library: there is no bits-per-key or FPR parameter, and no delete, serialization or merge.
how_it_is_fast: It is a split block Bloom filter, combining Putze et al.'s cache-blocked Bloom filter with Broder-Mitzenmacher split filters. One hash picks a 256-bit block, and one AVX2 multiply (_mm256_mullo_epi32 by eight odd constants, shift right 27) turns the rest into eight 5-bit indices that set one bit in each 32-bit lane. Insert is a single OR-store and lookup a single _mm256_testc_si256, so each operation touches one 32-byte-aligned block with a fixed, branch-free instruction count. A standard Bloom filter does k scattered memory probes instead, which is why the gap grows from about 2x at 10M keys to about 2.7-2.9x at 100M keys.
when_to_use: Read-heavy membership pre-checks (join or semi-join filters, skipping disk or LSM or Parquet-style reads) where a false-positive rate of roughly 0.4-19% is acceptable, the range its author gives. fastfilter_cpp's tuning notes put its lowest space overhead near 1-1.4% FPP.
Large filters that spill out of cache (10M-100M+ keys), where the single-block access pays off most: 20 ns vs 53-58 ns per query at 100M keys in the Xor Filters paper.
Insert-heavy or streaming construction: 10-20 ns/key vs 40-90 ns/key for standard Bloom. Unlike a cuckoo filter, Add never fails.
x86-64 servers with AVX2 (Haswell or later) whose keys are already 64-bit integers or 64-bit hashes.
As a ~140-line reference kernel to vendor. The same block scheme (identical salt constants) is standardized as Parquet's split block Bloom filter and is used in Impala, Kudu, Arrow and StarRocks.
when_not_to_use: You need a false-positive rate below about 0.4%. With a fixed 8 bits set per key, space grows fast: Parquet's SBBF table needs 16.9 bits/key for 0.1% and 26.4 for 0.01%, while an optimal standard Bloom filter needs 1.44*log2(1/eps), about 14.4 bits/key for 0.1%.

Memory is the binding constraint. In the paper it used 10.7 bits/key at 0.94% FPP, while Xor8 used 9.8 bits/key at 0.39%. The author's note says a standard Bloom filter reaches 0.63% in the space this filter needs for 1.0%.
You need deletes, counting, serialization, or OR-merging of filters. The hash seed is random per instance, so two filters built separately cannot be unioned.
Non-AVX2 x86, ARM, MSVC or Windows. The code uses AVX2 intrinsics, posix_memalign, unsigned __int128 and GCC builtins, and the constructor throws std::runtime_error on CPUs without AVX2.
You want maintained code. simd-block.h has not changed since Dec 2016 or the repo since Nov 2021, and PR #32 (a hashing change the author reports as 15% faster) was never merged.

integration.dependencies: OpenSSL headers, pulled in transitively by hashutil.h (#include <openssl/evp.h>) even though the filter does not use them. The repo Makefiles also link -lssl -lcrypto. The filter needs nothing else.
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (the repo builds with --std=c++11). Needs GCC or Clang extensions (__builtin_cpu_supports, [[gnu::always_inline]], unsigned __int128); MSVC support is not documented.
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 only (the benchmarks compile with -march=core-avx2), on POSIX systems (posix_memalign). fastfilter_cpp's derived SimdBlockFilterFixed adds aarch64 NEON and SSE4.1 variants.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. By code inspection, Find is const and read-only, so concurrent lookups on a finished filter are safe. Add does a non-atomic 256-bit load-OR-store, so concurrent Adds need external locking or they can lose bits, which causes false negatives.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same insert-only, false-positives-only semantics as a Bloom filter, but a different interface: the constructor takes log2(bytes), keys are uint64_t only, and there is no FPR/k parameter, union or serialization

gotchas: The move constructor copies directory_ without nulling the source's pointer, so both destructors free the same buffer if a move actually runs. Returning the filter by value, as the repo's benchmark does, only works because of copy elision.

Size is always 2^log_heap_space bytes, so bits/key and FPR jump with n. The repo's own benchmark, using the same sizing rule, shows 8.95-15.79 bits/item and 0.14%-2.07% FPR across runs. Overfilling degrades FPR silently rather than failing; Parquet's spec cites about 18% at 5 bits/key.

The default TwoIndependentMultiplyShift hash is seeded from std::random_device in every constructor, so filters are not reproducible across runs or processes and cannot be merged. It is only 2-independent, and the repo's random.h warns that multiply-shift behaves non-randomly on some structured inputs. The paper's benchmark used a Murmur finalizer instead.

Build flags: it needs -mavx2 (or -march) and, per its own comment, -fno-strict-aliasing, because of the __m256i reinterpret_casts. It also relies on transitive includes for memset and std::runtime_error, since there is no <cstring> or <stdexcept>.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over the Cuckoo Filter in the same repo when you never delete and can live with about 1% FPR: the repo's own benchmark shows 55-74M adds/sec vs 23-35M for Cuckoo8, and inserts cannot fail. Pick it over the Xor Filter or BuRR/Ribbon when keys arrive incrementally or build and query speed beat space (10 vs 110 ns/key build, 16 vs 23 ns query at 10M keys vs Xor8); pick those when bits/key matter.
verified_claims_summary: The Xor Filters paper (Graf & Lemire, ACM JEA 2020) benchmarked a modified copy of this kernel (fastfilter_cpp's SimdBlockFilterFixed: non-power-of-2 sizing, 10.7 bits/key, Murmur-finalizer hash) single-threaded with GCC 8.1.0 -O3 -march=native on an Intel i7-6700 Skylake at 3.4 GHz. With 25% of queries present it took 16 ns per query vs 31 ns (Bloom, 8 bits/key) and 40 ns (Bloom, 12 bits/key) at 10M keys, 20 ns vs 53/58 ns at 100M keys, and 10-20 vs 40-90 ns/key to build, at 0.94% FPP vs 2.2% (Bloom 8) and 0.31% (Bloom 12).
status_note: Abandoned (simd-block.h untouched since Dec 2016, repo since Nov 2021) but Apache-2.0 and about 140 lines, so easy to vendor; for maintained code, use the author's jbapple/libfilter (C/C++/Java/Go, last push Aug 2023, with an NDV/FPP sizing API) or fastfilter_cpp's non-power-of-2 variant.
